# Ghostyper

Prepared text typed with custom pace, pauses and corrections.

- Dates: 2026
- Status: macOS application
- Areas: Software engineering; Native apps; AI / ML
- Stack: Swift · AppKit · Accessibility · MLX
- Topics: Swift; macOS; Accessibility; Core Graphics; Automation; Productivity; Local-First Tools
- Public case study: https://mgiorgetti.com/project_details/project-ghoststroke.html

## Problem

Prepared text needs controlled insertion into another application, with configurable typing behavior and a clear way for the user to pause or stop it.

## Contribution

Native macOS application development, including destination selection, typing profiles, a test bench and optional local alternative-phrase generation.

## Technical approach and public case study

Type prepared text into the field you choose, with your own pace, pauses, and locally generated alternative phrases.

### Choose where to type.

Prepare the text, choose a profile, and select a destination.

- Prepare your text Write or paste into Quick Type, then choose a saved typing profile.

- Choose the destination Press Start, then ⇧ Shift ⌥ Option -click the field where it should go.

- Keep control Your keyboard or mouse input pauses typing. Resume by choosing where to continue, or stop from the panel, menu bar, or shortcut.

### Tune the typing profile

Fine-tune speed, thinking pauses, and mistakes. Save a profile and try it before sending text to another app.

#### See what comes next

Test Bench pairs a typing canvas with a timeline of upcoming pauses and corrections. Replay individual phrases as you adjust the profile.

#### Local alternative phrases

Optional local generation prepares false starts that are typed and erased before your original text.

## Results and limitations

The application targets Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later and requires Accessibility access. Some destination applications reject simulated typing. The portfolio animation uses a fixed example rather than running a local model in the browser.
